title: Small simplicial subspaces are presentable and filteredly exhaust a monomorphism
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and write $\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$, with simplicial sets as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $|B|=|\coprod_{p,q\geq0}B_{p,q}|$. All diagrams and Hom sets are small relative to $\mathcal U$. An infinite cardinal $\gamma$ is regular if unions of fewer than $\gamma$ sets of size less than $\gamma$ have size less than $\gamma$. A category is $\gamma$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\gamma$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\gamma$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\gamma$-filtered colimits, with colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every uncountable regular small cardinal $\gamma$ larger than the number of morphisms of $\Delta\times\Delta$, every arrow $A\to B$ in $\mathrm{sS}$ with $|A|,|B|<\gamma$ is $\gamma$-presentable as an object of the arrow category $\mathrm{sS}^{[1]}$. If $X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a monomorphism, the small poset $I_\gamma(Y)$ of simplicial subspaces $B\subseteq Y$ with $|B|<\gamma$, ordered by inclusion, is $\gamma$-filtered. The canonical cocone from the diagram $(X\cap B\hookrightarrow B)_{B\in I_\gamma(Y)}$ to $X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a colimit cocone in the arrow category. Subspaces and intersections are computed in every bidegree.

source.place: Agent-formulated bounded-presheaf presentation input to the auxiliary descendant Bousfield–Smith argument under ancestor proof paragraph 2. Not a literal statement of the ancestor blueprint. Presentability follows by the small category-of-elements presentation by representables for presheaves on the countable bisimplicial arrow indexing category; the filtered-union clause is the degreewise colimit construction. No specific Stacks tag for the cardinal-presentability assertion was identified.

proof.text: Put $D=[1]\times\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $[1]$ has the arrow $0\to1$. An arrow $A\to B$ of simplicial spaces is exactly a covariant Set-valued diagram $F:D\to\mathrm{Set}$: its values at $0$ are those of $A$, its values at $1$ those of $B$, and the mixed arrows express naturality of $A\to B$. Maps of diagrams are exactly commuting squares of bisimplicial maps. This follows by expanding the two functor laws and the naturality equations in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Colimits of such diagrams are computed at each $d\in D$: take the set colimits there, and induce each operator from the compatible component operators. A cocone to another diagram gives unique component maps by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; their naturality holds after every coprojection, hence by uniqueness. This verifies existence and the universal property, and shows evaluation at $d$ preserves all small colimits.

source.place: Agent argument, bounded-presheaf input: identification of the arrow category with diagrams and pointwise colimits.

proof.text: Fix the diagram $F$ for $A\to B$. Define a small category $E$ with objects $(d,x)$, $d\in D$, $x\in F(d)$, and arrows $(d,x)\to(e,y)$ the arrows $a:d\to e$ of $D$ such that $F(a)x=y$. Composition is that of $D$, well defined by functoriality; write $\pi:E\to D$ for the projection. Its object set is the disjoint union of the elements of $A$ and $B$, so has size less than $\gamma$. The morphisms of $D$ are three copies of the morphisms of $\Delta\times\Delta$, so also have size less than $\gamma$. A morphism of $E$ is determined by its source element and its projected arrow. For each source element there are fewer than $\gamma$ choices, and there are fewer than $\gamma$ source elements. Regularity therefore gives $|\operatorname{Mor}E|<\gamma$. This includes the case $F$ is empty, when $E$ is empty.

source.place: Agent argument, bounded-presheaf input: explicit category of elements and its cardinal bound.

proof.text: For any diagram $G:D\to\mathrm{Set}$, a map $F\to G$ is a family $t_{d,x}\in G(d)$ satisfying $G(a)t_{d,x}=t_{e,F(a)x}$ for every $a:d\to e$. Indeed a natural transformation $u$ gives $t_{d,x}=u_d(x)$; conversely define $u_d(x)=t_{d,x}$ and these equations give its naturality. These operations are inverse, including empty fibers. The displayed families are exactly the limit of $G\pi:E\to\mathrm{Set}$. They identify the functor $\operatorname{Hom}(F,-)$ with the pointwise limit of the evaluation functors $\mathrm{ev}_{\pi(e)}$, indexed by $E$. Postcomposing $G\to G'$ applies its component to each $t_{d,x}$, so this identification is natural in $G$. Each evaluation preserves small $\gamma$-filtered colimits by step 1. Since $E$ has fewer than $\gamma$ morphisms, [lem-coef-accessible-set-functor-limits] says that their pointwise limit preserves these colimits. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(F,-)$ preserves them. Via step 1 this proves the required $\gamma$-presentability of the arbitrary arrow $A\to B$.

source.place: Agent argument, bounded-presheaf input: Hom as a small limit of evaluation functors and the existing Mathlib commutation theorem.

proof.text: A subspace $B\subseteq Y$ means subsets $B_{p,q}\subseteq Y_{p,q}$ stable under both simplicial directions. Such families form a subset of the powerset of $\coprod_{p,q}Y_{p,q}$, so $I_\gamma(Y)$ is small. The empty family is a subspace and has size zero. For a family $(B_i)_{i\in T}$ with $|T|<\gamma$, the union $B_{p,q}=\bigcup_i(B_i)_{p,q}$ is stable under every operator: an element comes from one $B_i$, and its operator stays in that $B_i$. Its total set is a union of fewer than $\gamma$ sets of size less than $\gamma$, hence has size less than $\gamma$ by regularity. This gives an upper bound, including the empty family. A category with fewer than $\gamma$ morphisms has fewer than $\gamma$ objects, by its identity arrows; thus every diagram of that size in this poset has an upper bound on its objects, which is a cocone because a poset has at most one arrow between any two objects. This proves $\gamma$-filteredness.

source.place: Agent argument, filtered-union input: smallness, unions, regularity and the empty diagram.

proof.text: Every $y\in Y_{p,q}$ lies in a subspace of size less than $\gamma$. In bidegree $(r,s)$ take all images $Y(\alpha,\beta)y$ for order-preserving $\alpha:[r]\to[p]$ and $\beta:[s]\to[q]$. Identities include $y$ and composition of operators makes these subsets a subspace. Its total set is an image of a subset of $\operatorname{Mor}(\Delta\times\Delta)$, so has size less than $\gamma$. Consequently $\bigcup_{B\in I_\gamma(Y)}B=Y$. Identify the monomorphism $X\hookrightarrow Y$ with its degreewise subset. Then $(X\cap B)_{p,q}=X_{p,q}\cap B_{p,q}$ is stable under operators and these intersections have degreewise union $X$. This identification also explains the intersection convention in the statement.

source.place: Agent argument, filtered-union input: the subspace generated by a simplex and exhaustion of both endpoints.

proof.text: Verify the arrow-colimit property directly. Given a cocone of squares from $(X\cap B\hookrightarrow B)$ to a fixed arrow $h:U\to V$, denote its component maps by $u_B:X\cap B\to U$ and $v_B:B\to V$. For $y\in Y_{p,q}$ choose a bounded $B$ containing it and put $v(y)=v_B(y)$. For $x\in X_{p,q}$ choose such a $B$ and put $u(x)=u_B(x)$. These values are independent of choices: $B\cup B'$ is a bounded subspace by step 4, and cocone compatibility identifies both values there. For any simplicial operator, use a $B$ containing the original simplex; it contains its image, and naturality of $u_B,v_B$ proves naturality of $u,v$. For $x\in X\cap B$, the square equation gives $hu(x)=v(x)$, hence $(u,v)$ is a square. It restricts to the given cocone and is unique since every simplex occurs in some $B$ by step 5. This is exactly the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], proving the final assertion for the specified canonical cocone.

source.place: Agent argument, filtered-union input: explicit universal property of the canonical arrow cocone.
